reason: The current goal is to flip the deck, so I’ll do that first.
expectation: I expect to see the underside of the deck, ready for fittings.

alternatives.reason: A wheel can be fitted to a motor, but flipping follows the stated goal.

reaction: The change of face is clear, though the bare board is not especially distinctive.
reason: I’ll follow the stated goal and fit a wheel to the left motor.
expectation: I expect the wheel to attach to the left motor’s shaft.

alternatives.reason: The other wheel also appears suitable; I chose the first one arbitrarily.

reaction: The wheel and projecting lead make the new drive easy to distinguish.
reason: I’ll follow the goal and fit the remaining wheel to the right motor.
expectation: I expect a right drive with the wheel on its motor shaft.

alternatives.reason: I could mount the left drive now, but the goal calls for preparing the right one first.

reaction: The right drive's screws and lead give a clear picture of the assembly.
reason: I’ll follow the goal and mount the left drive on the deck.
expectation: I expect the left motor and wheel to attach to one side of the deck.

alternatives.reason: The right drive can also be mounted, but the goal specifies the left first.

reaction: The added wheel and motor make the deck look more like a vehicle.
reason: I’ll follow the goal and mount the right drive.
expectation: I expect the second motor and wheel to attach to the rover.

effect: Both drives are mounted, and the next goal is to fit the caster.
reaction: The second wheel makes the vehicle layout clearer.

reaction: The round foot is a distinct addition, though its support role is not obvious from this view.
reason: I’ll follow the goal and fit the battery pack to power the rover.
expectation: I expect the blue battery case to attach to the board; its electrical connection may come later.

effect: The battery pack is fitted; the receiver is the next goal.
reaction: The dark-topped box is a visible addition, although it is described as green rather than the expected blue.
reason: I’ll fit the receiver, following the goal and the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the receiver box to attach to the rover; I’m unsure whether its wiring will also be connected.

effect: The receiver is fitted and the rover chapter is complete; the final picture distinguishes the blue case from the closed green box, but does not clarify wiring.
reaction: The completed layout is recognizable, though there is no motion shown as a final payoff.

mostWorthwhile.text: Mounting the second drive made the two-wheel vehicle layout clear and gave the construction a recognizable form.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the battery was less clear: the result described a dark-topped green box rather than the expected blue case.

surprise.text: The battery fitting produced a green-box description, while the completed rover described both a blue case and a closed green box.

arbitrary.text: Choosing between the two wheels for the left motor was arbitrary because both were offered and appeared interchangeable.

continue.text: I probably would not continue immediately: the instructions were clear and the physical additions mostly distinct, but the repetitive fittings and lack of a motion payoff made this chapter less compelling.
